summary: Round 2 audit after the CC3 Testnet deployment and the 3D/motion UI wave. Screenshots of every route of the local dev server and the hosted site at 1440x900 and 390x844 were judged, console output collected, and README, docs, deck, KittyLedger.sol, the worker and the web app were read. The project is strong: contracts, worker, tests and docs are consistent in almost every detail, the testnet round is real and the dashboard reads it. What now costs points is the gap between the story and the live evidence: (1) the testnet log's rows are appended into the wrong markdown table so the explorer links are invisible on GitHub; (2) the flagship claim 'settles a whole round in one precompile call' is contradicted by the live log (batch of 1, then batch of 2) because the policy fires on a 45-second timer before roundmates are attested; (3) the hosted site still calls http://localhost:8790 and prints CORS errors on /lab and /steward; (4) the attack-lab testnet record landed mid-audit (commit 782f5a8, 7 of 8 pass) but the late scenario is still skipped, the local fallback recording is unlabelled, and that commit swept two audit temp scripts into the repo; (5) the demo video, runbook, README screenshots and deck slide 4 all describe the local world. On UX: round numbers mix 0- and 1-indexing on the circle page, three real mobile defects exist (a tag that forces horizontal scroll on /steward, a clipped round timeline, no hero visual under 640px), and the 3D scenes read as competent but plastic (flat-lit standard materials, no environment reflections, no grounding shadows, a hero that invents random pulses, and a flow scene that loops fake traffic instead of the chain). On Attestcoin depth the ledger is already deep; two tightenings remain (bound startHeight against the attested frontier at creation to close a consent-griefing hole, and record the attestation that proved a deadline when a miss is written), both requiring a redeploy so they are bundled and ranked below the truth fixes. Items are ordered by expected score gain per hour.

items.title: Fix docs/TESTNET_LOG.md: the testnet rows are in a 3-column table so GitHub hides the tx links and gas
items.problem: README (Deployments paragraph, line ~236), SUBMISSION.md and deck slide 9 all say 'Every transaction is linked in docs/TESTNET_LOG.md'. In the file, the main table (header `| date | chain | action | tx | gas used |`) is empty, and the sixteen 5-cell testnet rows (deploy KittyLedger ... confirmPayout round 0) were appended by `pnpm txlog` to the END of the file, i.e. under the 3-column 'Sepolia deployments' table (`| date | contract | address |`). GFM drops cells beyond the header count, so on GitHub every testnet row renders as `2026-09-12 | Creditcoin CC3 Testnet | deploy KittyLedger` with NO explorer link and NO gas. The one piece of evidence a judge is pointed at is invisible. Cause: worker/src/txlog.ts line 35 does `fs.writeFileSync(file, md + row)` (append at EOF).
items.fix: 1) docs/TESTNET_LOG.md: move the sixteen `| 2026-09-12 | ... |` rows (from `deploy KittyLedger` through `confirmPayout round 0`) up under the main 5-column header, in the order they occur; leave the three Sepolia deployment rows (TestUSD, KittyVault, FakeVault) in the 3-column table. Add a one-line summary above the table: 'Circle #1 Delhi Chit Circle · round 0: 3 Sepolia payments → 2 batch proofs (1 + 2, see docs/audit-round-2.json item 2) → early close → 300 tUSD payout → proof-back. Round 1 in progress.' 2) worker/src/txlog.ts: replace the EOF append with an insert after the main table header: find the index of the line `|---|---|---|---|---|` that follows `| date | chain | action | tx | gas used |`, then find the end of that table (first blank line after it) and insert the row there; keep the console message. 3) Also append rows for round 1 as it happens (`pnpm txlog sepolia 0x2e6f… "contribute round 1 member 0"` etc.).
items.verify: Open https://github.com/Prashant-thakur77/Kitty/blob/main/docs/TESTNET_LOG.md: the first table shows 16+ rows each with a clickable explorer link and a gas figure. `pnpm txlog creditcoin <hash> "test"` inserts inside the first table, not at EOF (then remove the test row).

items.title: Make 'a whole round in one precompile call' true on testnet: hold a batch for attested roundmates, then settle round 1 as a batch of 3
items.problem: The first bold bullet in README (line 19) and SUBMISSION.md, and deck slide 5, say the ledger 'settles a whole round in one precompile call'. The live steward log (web/src/data/steward.sample.json, shown on the hosted /steward) shows round 0 settled in two calls: `proving 1 payment(s) ... waited 239s for a fuller batch` with `stillWaitingForAttestation=2`, then `proving 2 payment(s) ... waited 373s`. Members 1 and 2 had paid 2–4 Sepolia blocks after member 0 but were not yet attested; `decideBatch` fired on `reason: 'waited'` (WORKER_BATCH_WAIT_MS default 45s, worker/src/config.ts line 29) despite `blocksOfSlack=227`. The policy's own doc string says 'thrift wins over impatience', but the timer overrides thrift whenever the attestation frontier lags. A judge who reads the log next to the claim sees the contradiction.
items.fix: 1) worker/src/agent/policy.ts: add `export const ATTESTATION_LAG_BLOCKS = 64` and a new hold rule inside `decideBatch`, applied only when the computed reason would be `'waited'`: for every (circleId, round) present in `batch`, count payments in `pending` for the same circle+round that are NOT provable (`p.block > frontier.attestedHeight`); if that count is > 0 and `bestSlack > URGENT_BLOCKS + ATTESTATION_LAG_BLOCKS`, set `reason = 'wait'` and add `heldForRoundmates: <count>` and `holdUntilAttested: <max block of those roundmates>` to `evidence`. `explainBatch` for `!d.act` gains a third branch: `waiting: ${e.queries} query(ies) ready but ${e.heldForRoundmates} roundmate payment(s) not yet attested (need source block ${e.holdUntilAttested}); ${e.blocksOfSlack} blocks of slack, holding for one call`. Keep `deadline-risk`, `round-complete`, `full` and `forced` unchanged so urgency still wins. 2) worker/test/policy.test.ts: add `test('holds a provable payment while roundmates are unattested and slack is ample')` (3 members, blocks 100/102/104, frontier attestedHeight 101, closeHeight 400, waitMs 0 → act=false, evidence.heldForRoundmates=2) and `test('does not hold when slack is short')` (closeHeight 150 → act=true, reason 'deadline-risk'). 3) Update the 26→28 agent-test count in README Quick start and the '14 unit tests' figure in the Steward table. 4) Round 1 on testnet: member 0 already paid on Sepolia (block 11,686,729). Before starting `pnpm worker`, have members 1 and 2 pay (`pnpm demo contribute --skip 0`), then run the worker so the log shows ONE `recordContributions round 1 (batch of 3)`; `pnpm txlog` it. If round 1's deadline (Sepolia 11,686,925) has already passed by then, record it honestly as late payments (−20 each) — that is a fine demo of the score — and settle round 2 as the clean batch of 3. 5) Wording until the batch-of-3 row exists: README line 19 and SUBMISSION → 'Settles up to ten payments from every open circle in one precompile call' and add to the Deployments paragraph: 'Round 0 landed in two calls (1 + 2) because the steward's batch timer fired before two payments were attested; the policy now holds for attested roundmates.' Refresh web/src/data/steward.sample.json from worker/state after round 1 so the hosted log shows the hold decisions.
items.verify: `pnpm test:agent` passes with the two new tests. After round 1: docs/TESTNET_LOG.md has one `recordContributions round 1 (batch of 3, verified by 0x0FD2)` row; the hosted /steward shows a `wait` entry with `heldForRoundmates=2` followed by one `prove` with `queries=3` and `roundsCompleted=1`.

'http://localhost:8790' : '')`. 2) Lab.tsx and Steward.tsx: in the `useEffect`, if `!cfg.labApi` set `offline=true` and call `loadRecorded()` / `loadSample()` directly without any fetch; guard `run()` and `ask()` the same way. 3) The 'Ask the steward · Layer 3' form on the hosted page: replace the disabled input+button with a static example answer block rendered from a committed `web/src/data/steward.explain.sample.json` (record one real `pnpm explain "why did you prove one payment alone?"` answer against the testnet log, including its `verified` and `stripped` arrays) so a judge sees Layer 3 and the citation validator working instead of a disabled button.

items.title: Finish the attack-lab record: run the late scenario after round 1's deadline, label the local recording, remove dead Run buttons, drop the swept-in temp scripts
items.problem: Commit 782f5a8 (landed during this audit) committed web/public/lab-testnet.json with 7 of 8 scenarios passing on the live precompile (wrongChain rejected by 0x0FD2 itself) and made Lab.tsx render skipped results in amber, which backs deck slide 9 once GitHub Pages redeploys. Remaining gaps: `late` is `skipped: deadline 11686925 not passed yet on Sepolia`, so the hosted page will show one amber card; web/public/lab-recorded.json (the local-anvil fallback) has no `mode` field, so whenever the testnet file fails to load the page labels a local run only `recorded run · 2026-09-11 · f30433d` beside a header reading Sepolia 11,686,7xx; the eight disabled `Run live (needs pnpm lab:api)` buttons are dead affordances on a hosted page; and the same commit swept two audit temp scripts (scripts/media/_tmp_audit_shots.mjs, scripts/media/_tmp_audit_extra.mjs) into the repo — they are deleted in the worktree but still tracked.
items.fix: 1) Once Sepolia head > 11,686,925 (round 1 deadline) and before the round is closed, record only the late scenario into the testnet file (LAB_ONLY=late, LAB_RECORD_OUT=web/public/lab-testnet.json, WORKER_STATE_FILE=state.testnet.json, pnpm -s lab:record): a member who has not paid pays late, the ledger accepts it with onTime=false and a real −20 lands on a real score; add the Sepolia tx to docs/TESTNET_LOG.md with pnpm txlog ("contribute round 1 member N (late)") and commit the JSON. If round 1 closes first, do it in round 2. 2) web/src/pages/Lab.tsx: when `recorded && recorded.mode !== 'testnet'` the tag text becomes `recorded on two local anvils · precompiles mocked` (tone amber); when `offline`, do not render the per-card Run button at all and add one header line `Reproduce: pnpm scenarios (local, ~3 min) · pnpm lab:record (testnet)`. 3) Re-run pnpm lab:record against the local world (KITTY_ENV_FILE=worker/.env.world) so lab-recorded.json carries `mode: "local"` (record-lab.ts already writes it). 4) Stage the removal of the two _tmp_audit_*.mjs files (git rm) in the next commit; they are audit scratch.
items.verify: Hosted /lab shows eight mint cards (no amber/red), tag `recorded on Sepolia + CC3 Testnet`, no Run buttons, and lines with explorer links; `git ls-files scripts/media | grep _tmp` prints nothing; lab-recorded.json contains `"mode": "local"`.

items.title: One round-numbering convention across the circle page, feed, timeline and steward
items.problem: On the hosted /circle/1 a judge sees, in one viewport: header tag `round 2 of 3`, band eyebrow `ROUND 2 OF 3`, section title `Members · round 1` (Circle.tsx: `Members · round ${circle.currentRound}`), timeline discs labelled 0/1/2 (RotationWheel.tsx line 242 `String(r)`), feed rows `Round 1 open`, `Round 0 closed` (hooks.ts lines 102–103), the wheel centre `ROUND 2 OF 3`, and the steward log `round=0`. Mixed 0- and 1-indexing in the same screen makes the live state look wrong ('round 2 of 3 … 0 of 3 proven … Round 1 open').
items.fix: Adopt: human labels are 1-indexed everywhere in the UI; the on-chain index is shown as a mono chip `r0` only where a hash-level reader needs it (Score history already uses `r0`). Changes: Circle.tsx section title → `Members · round ${circle.currentRound + 1} of ${n}` and the list heading `round ${r}` in the 'show as list' view → `round ${r + 1}`; RotationWheel.tsx disc text `String(r)` → `String(r + 1)`; hooks.ts feed text: `Round ${a.round + 1} closed →` / `Round ${a.round + 1} open ·` and add ` (r${a.round})` at the end of those two strings; ProvePanel/steward copy that says 'round 0' in web/src/data/steward.sample.json stays (it is the worker's log) but Steward.tsx `SAMPLE_QUESTION` → 'Why did you prove one payment alone?' since no round 1 has been closed. Add a one-line note in the Round history section: 'Rounds are numbered 1…n here; contracts and logs use the 0-based index rN.'

PLACEHOLDER} … loading={false} />` in a 260px box under the CTA row instead of the empty `.streak` div — it is the same object as the 3D circle, costs nothing extra (already in the bundle), and looks like the product. items.title: 3D premium pass: environment reflections, physical materials, grounding, and choreography driven only by real chain events
items.problem: Both scenes are solid but read as 'plastic': `meshStandardMaterial` under two directional lights with no environment map, so the pot torus and coins have no reflections and the slabs in FlowScene are flat dark boxes with aliased 1-px EdgesGeometry outlines. The coins are anonymous flat-shaded cylinders while every other surface in the app identifies members with a Blockie. Nothing casts a contact shadow, so objects float. Choreography: HeroScene spawns a random `in` pulse every 9 s of idle (`if (s.idle > 9 …) spawn('in', Math.floor(Math.random() * n))`) — on a product whose tagline is 'proven, not promised' the hero invents payments that did not happen; FlowScene is a fixed loop (`PACKET_EVERY = 2.3`, `TICK_EVERY = 6.5`) unrelated to the chain even though the page has `useAttestation` and `useLedgerEvents`. Console shows `THREE.Clock: This module has been deprecated` on every 3D page (r3f 9.7 on three 0.186). Bundle: the three chunk is 234 KB gz; keep it flat.
items.fix: Materials/lighting (both scenes): in Stage.tsx `onCreated`, build `new PMREMGenerator(state.gl).fromScene(new RoomEnvironment(), 0.04).texture` (import `RoomEnvironment` from 'three/examples/jsm/environments/RoomEnvironment.js', ~3 KB) and set `state.scene.environment = tex` with `state.scene.environmentIntensity = 0.35`; switch pot torus, coin faces and slab tops to `meshPhysicalMaterial` with `clearcoat 1, clearcoatRoughness 0.15, roughness 0.28, metalness 0.55` (pot) / `metalness 0.75, roughness 0.35` (coins); drop the second directional light's intensity to 0.6. Grounding: add a single `<ContactShadows frames={1} opacity={0.5} blur={2.2} scale={7} position={[0,-0.07,0]} />` (drei is already a dependency; `frames={1}` renders once). Identity: give each coin a `CanvasTexture` of its member's Blockie — extract the pixel generator from ui.tsx `Blockie` into `web/src/lib/blockie.ts` returning an 8×8 colour grid, draw it at 64×64 with `imageSmoothingEnabled=false`, apply as `map` on the coin's top face (use a `CylinderGeometry` with separate top material via material array), so the 3D circle shows the same three identicons as the member list. Choreography: delete the idle random spawn; instead pass `attested` from `useAttestation()` as a prop and when it increases run a one-off sweep of the 48 outer ticks (light each tick in order over 1.2 s, tick material `color` lerp to mint) — an attestation is a real event and this is its only visual anywhere. On `BatchVerified` spawn `count` pulses simultaneously (not 0.45 s apart) so 'one call' is what the eye sees; on `PayoutConfirmed` leave a persistent thin mint ring around the recipient coin (read `rounds` → `receivedPot`). FlowScene: accept `{ attested, items }` props from Architecture.tsx (call the two hooks there); fire the amber tick only when `attested` changes and packets only for new `ContributionRecorded` items (replay the last 3 on mount for a first impression, then real ones); add a small `Html` counter on the ledger slab `${proven} proven` from `useGlobalStats`. Replace `EdgesGeometry` outlines with a 0.02-thick emissive rim mesh (`BoxGeometry(3.04,0.02,1.94)` at the slab top, `meshBasicMaterial`) to remove aliasing. Silence the Clock warning by upgrading `@react-three/fiber` to the release that uses `THREE.Timer` (or pin three to the r3f peer range). Budget: after `pnpm --dir web build`, the `events-*.js` chunk must stay ≤ 245 KB gz (it is 234 KB now).
items.verify: Screenshot hosted landing at 1440x900: coins show identicons and specular highlights, a soft shadow under the pot; no console warnings from three; `ls -la web/dist/assets | grep events` size within budget; with the worker stopped, the hero stays still except for the attestation sweep when the nav's attested number increments.

items.title: Ledger tightening (one redeploy): bound startHeight against the attested frontier, and record the attestation that proved every missed deadline
items.problem: Two gaps a careful reviewer will find. (1) Consent griefing: `_initCircle` (KittyLedger.sol lines 747–772) accepts any `startHeight`. An organiser can open an invite circle whose round-0 close height is already attested; invitees who redeem consent (`_join(..., true)`), the organiser calls `closeInvites`, and anyone calls `closeRound` immediately: every invitee is written `missed` (−120) for a round that never existed for them. The registry check `get_chain_by_key` is there but the frontier is not consulted. (2) Auditability of misses: `closeRound` (lines 418–433) gates on `is_height_attested(chainKey, closeAt)` but stores nothing about WHICH attestation proved the deadline; `ContributionMissed(circleId, round, member, deadlineHeight)` carries only the deadline. The README claims 'every input is a proven transaction or an attested deadline', yet a lender re-checking a miss has no attestation height/hash to verify. Both are cheap, both deepen ChainInfo usage on the hot path (6 of 11 functions), and both change the ABI, so they need a redeploy — do them together, and only if there is time for one more settled round after redeploying (round takes ~20 min).
items.fix: (1) In `_initCircle`, after the registry check: `IChainInfo.HeightHash memory latest = CHAIN_INFO.get_latest_attestation_height_and_hash(chainKey); if (latest.exists && startHeight + roundBlocks <= latest.height) revert InvalidCircle("round 0 already attested");` — round 0's deadline must lie beyond the attested frontier. Add `test_createCircle_revertsWhenRound0DeadlineAlreadyAttested` (setAttestedHeight(CHAIN_KEY, START + ROUND_BLOCKS) then createCircle → revert) and `test_redeemInvite_cannotBeGriefedByPastStart` in KittyInvites.t.sol; scan existing tests that call `setAttestedHeight` before `createCircle` (KittyMultiChain.t.sol lines 175–179, KittyCreditLine.t.sol 151, KittyViewer.t.sol 107/193) and, where a fixture creates a circle after raising the frontier, use a later START. (2) Add to `struct Round`: `uint64 attestedCloseHeight; bytes32 attestedCloseHash;`. In `closeRound`, inside the `if (rd.contributions < n)` branch after the `is_height_attested` check: `IChainInfo.HeightHash memory a = CHAIN_INFO.find_lowest_attested_after(c.chainKey, closeAt); rd.attestedCloseHeight = a.height; rd.attestedCloseHash = a.hash;` and extend the events: `ContributionMissed(circleId, round, member, deadlineHeight, attestedHeight, attestedHash)` and `RoundClosed(..., attestedHeight)`. Test: `test_closeRound_recordsAttestationEvidence` asserting the stored height/hash equal the mock's `_hash`. (3) Regenerate web ABIs (`forge build` + the copy step in scripts/deploy.sh), show `attested @ <height> · <hash…>` on Score.tsx history rows of kind ContributionMissed and in the ProofFeed text for RoundClosed; add both functions to the Protocol coverage table in docs/ATTESTCOIN_INTEGRATION.md and change 'Five of the ChainInfo precompile's eleven functions' to six (README table row 'Attestation bounds' likewise). (4) Redeploy with `scripts/deploy.sh` (new KittyLedger address → deployments.json, web/.env.production, README Deployments table, SUBMISSION.md, deck slide 9), keep the old address in TESTNET_LOG.md under 'v1 ledger (round 0 evidence)', and run the batch-of-3 round from item 2 on the new ledger.
items.verify: `forge test` → 106 passing (103 + 3); `cast call <newLedger> "getRound(uint256,uint32)" 1 1 --rpc-url https://rpc.cc3-testnet.creditcoin.network` returns a non-zero attestedCloseHeight for any round closed on the deadline path; `cast send … createCircle(...)` with `startHeight` 1000 reverts with `InvalidCircle("round 0 already attested")`.

items.title: Deck: replace text-only slides with the live testnet, fix slide overflow, reprint the PDF
items.problem: All twelve slides are bullet text on a dark background; the only 'proof' slide (9) is four bullets. Slide 4 'Live loop' still narrates the LOCAL demo ('round 1 one member misses; … the score drops from 515 to 395') — nothing like that happened on testnet. Slide 11 says '26 agent tests' (will be 28 after item 2). The slide container overflows the 900px viewport by 61px (`.slide { min-height: 100vh; padding: 48px }` under a fixed nav), so every slide shows a scrollbar on a 1440x900 projector. The deck is the artefact judges keep open while scoring; it should show the product and the chain, not describe them.
items.fix: Presentation.tsx: (a) Slide 4 → 'The first circle, live' with a two-column layout: left, `<RotationWheel …>` fed by `useCircle(1n)`/`useRoundDetail` (the components already exist and read the testnet); right, six live `Stat`s from the chain — circles, payments proven, batches, tUSD settled (from `useGlobalStats`), latest attested Sepolia block (`useAttestation`), KittyLedger address as a Blockscout link. (b) Slide 9 keeps the text but adds a compact table of the five key tx hashes (createCircle, recordContributions batch, closeRound, payout, confirmPayout) as explorer links (copy from docs/TESTNET_LOG.md) and, once item 2 lands, the 'batch of 3' row. (c) Slide 5 gets a right-hand code block quoting KittyLedger.sol lines 484–495 (`verifyAndEmit … BatchVerified`) so the depth claim points at real code. (d) Slide 7: embed the last three entries of steward.sample.json rendered with the same `Tag`+evidence chips as /steward. (e) Slide 11: compute the test counts from constants in one place (`const COUNTS = { forge: 103, agent: 28, scenarios: 8 }`) and reuse in README via a comment. index.css: `.slide { min-height: calc(100vh - 64px); padding: 40px 48px }` (nav height 64) and keep the print rule. Reprint with `node scripts/media/deck.mjs` and re-upload docs/Kitty-deck.pdf to the release.
items.verify: Playwright /presentation at 1440x900: `document.documentElement.scrollHeight === 900` on slide 1; slide 4 shows the wheel with three identicons and non-zero stats read from the chain (network requests to rpc.cc3-testnet.creditcoin.network visible); `pdfinfo docs/Kitty-deck.pdf` reports 12 pages and page 4 contains the word 'Delhi'.
